newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Wool Board reports NZ$100,000 1995/6 deficit.
newsitem.headline: NZ Wool Board reports NZ$100,000 1995/6 deficit.

text.p: The New Zealand Wool Board on Wednesday reported a NZ$100,000 deficit for the 1995/96 season, and forecast it would slide to a NZ$15.9 million deficit for the coming year.
The board said its prediction for the 1996/97 year was based on an average clean price of 500 cents per kilogram, just below the average price for the last 10 years.

Chairman Pat Morrison said the board had ended the financial year in a sound position, with a "near break-even" result. This was achieved despite a reduction in levy income of NZ$11.2 million for the year. Levies were cut to five percent from six

Wools of New Zealand manager of economics and market information Patrick Conway said wool prices were expected to improve gradually over the coming season. However, he said a run-down in grower and trade stocks in the first part of the season would moderate any increases.
"An improvement in the economic outlook in our major markets will lead to increased trade demand as processors rebuild stocks," Conway said.
He said while growers selling in the first half of the season may receive lower prices than at the same time last year, prices in the second half were expected to be better.

His forecasts allowed for continued appreciation of the New Zealand dollar as a result of the Reserve Bank's tight monetary policy. This would continue to increase the cost of New Zealand wool to overseas customers, suppressing demand and lowering prices received by growers.
